added.question: Does the latch of F11 set on the enable node's low level, or on its falling edge? With a level set, a clear given while the enable is low leaves the gates disabled, and so does a clear control held or stuck closed. With an edge set, a clear given while the panel is stopped lets the gates return when the edges resume, with no operator action at that moment. Answer level or falling edge, and say which input wins when set and clear are both active.
added.why: The answer fixes the latch element: a set-dominant latch fed by the level, or an edge-triggered flip-flop with a clear. It also fixes whether its set overrides its clear. STATUS.md:340 holds that nothing re-arms on its own. P2 cannot qualify the latch without it. Question 0 asks the power-up state only.

added.question: How does the coprocessor's overcurrent and over-temperature action open the ESC pack switches? The options are an RP2354B output on a second, disable-only input of each switch driver, or no switch action at all: the throttle stops, and the switches follow the enable node alone. IOBoard.md:475 and the R8 row time the path 'from detection to the ESC pack switch open'. The R3 row says R3's gates follow the enable node alone. IOBoard.md:197 puts no processor in the path from GPIO6 to a gate.
added.why: A second input changes the driver's logic to an AND of the enable node and an RP2354B output. It adds an input under the powered-off isolation rule, and its level during an RP2354B reset decides whether the pack switches open through that reset, which the R3 row says they do not. P2 cannot qualify the onboard driver or the external module's driver output without it. P5 cannot budget the motor overcurrent path without it.

added.question: What inductance, in µH, do the leads between each ESC pack switch and the ESC have? When a high-side switch opens at full current, that inductance keeps the current flowing into the ESC's input capacitance. That drives the switched node negative until a clamp conducts. The energy is 0.5 x L x I²: 11 mJ at 1 µH and 150 A. The INA238 takes -0.3 V at least on VBUS, IN+ and IN- (SLYS025B section 5.1, https://www.ti.com/lit/ds/symlink/ina238.pdf, read 2026-09-28T10:40:16Z).
added.why: Question 18 covers only the pack-side leads, which set the positive transient. Without the switched side's inductance, P2 cannot size the clamp on the switched node or the MOSFETs' avalanche energy during turn-off. P5 cannot check the INA238 where it sits on the switched side; the shunt's side is not stated (IOBoard.md:469).

added.question: What lowest servo rail voltage, in V, does the servo rail gate close and conduct at? The rail has two settings, up to 5.5 V and up to 8.4 V, set from software (hardware/STATUS.md:37). The TPS55285 programs 0.8 V to 15 V (SLVSI72A, https://www.ti.com/lit/ds/symlink/tps55285.pdf, read 2026-09-28T10:40:16Z).
added.why: A high-side switch has a lowest supply at which its driver turns it fully on. P2 cannot pass or fail the gate's supply range, or a P-channel gate's drive, without the lowest rail voltage.
